To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TNF-α stimulates tyrosine phosphorylated proteins and that tyrosine kinase activity mediates TNF-α-induced upregulation of ICAM-1, E-selectin and neutrophil-endothelial adhesion.
tumor necrosis factor-α upregulation of intercellular adhesin molecule-1 and E-selection and subsequent neutrophil adhesin is mediated by protein tyrosine kinases in endothelial cells.

tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)-induced upregulation of ICAM-1 (intercellular adhesion molecule 2) and E-selecting expression, and consequent neutropil adhesion to human aortic endothelium in vitro, are suppressed by tyrosinase kinase inhibitors, including the isoflavone genistein, suggesting that TNF-α-induced protein tyrosine phosphorlyation is involved in these processes.

the role of protein kinase inhibitors in the upregualtion of ICAM-1, E-selectin and neutrophil-endothelium adhesion.
the role of protein kinase C in the upregulatory effect of TNF-α on the adhesion molecule ICAM-1.
the role of protein-tyrosine phosphorylation and the tyrosine kinase in endothelial cell function.
